title: feat: cookie consent with region-aware banner, blocker and cookie policy
body:
## What changed

Adds the cookie consent MVP that replaces Complianz:

- **Blocker** (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`): output buffer that holds back scripts and iframes from 23 known services (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-services.php`), plus owner-added patterns; embeds get a same-size placeholder with a Load button. Unknown third-party script hosts are recorded (up to 20) for the settings card.
- **Consent feature** (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`): settings, banner and Cookie settings dialog (`includes/views/consent-banner.php`), footer menu link, button, block and shortcode, `#cookie-settings` links, Complianz one-off import.
- **Browser** (`assets/js/spcc-head.js`, `assets/js/spcc.js`): region model from the time zone (opt-in for Europe, Quebec and unclear; opt-out elsewhere; quiet option), GPC, Google Consent Mode v2, WP Consent API, release in document order, cookie removal and reload when consent is taken back. A Load button allows one service without answering the banner (`p: 1` in the cookie).
- **Cookie policy feature** (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php`): block and `[spcc_cookie_policy]` listing detected services' cookies; privacy policy guide text.
- **Styles** (`assets/css/spcc.css`): Kadence palette and block theme tokens, bottom bar or corner box, mobile bottom sheet, 44px targets, reduced motion.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture.md`, README, readme.txt, changelogs, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md` → Front end; uninstall removes the seen list.

## Why

Complianz needs a scan, a wizard and upkeep. This works when switched on, keeps the HTML the same for every visitor (page caches), and asks only as strictly as each region needs. Defaults are configurable and not legal advice.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all stages pass (PHP, JS, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan).
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.3) and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4`: pass, no PHP messages, both features on. The seen list is autoloaded from the first page, so no per-page lookup.
- Playwright on a test site with GA, Meta Pixel, YouTube and Google Maps:
  - Europe/London: banner names all four services; nothing loads; Consent Mode default denied; dialog rows by category; Escape closes; Load video loads YouTube only and the banner stays (also after reload); Reject all then reloads and removes it.
  - Europe/Berlin: Accept all loads everything; Reject all from Cookie settings reloads and stops it.
  - Europe/Paris: Statistics only loads GA alone.
  - America/New_York: loads with a short notice; America/Chicago with GPC: marketing off.
  - Tab order: banner before the skip link; no JS errors in any scenario.
  - Mobile and simulated Kadence dark palette screenshots reviewed.
- Admin: Consent card lists found services by category and unknown hosts; region labels fit the select.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors. Warnings left are release-time items (Unreleased changelog sections, the WordPress.org slug note, the starter's banner, icon and screenshots) and one false positive: `.spcc-panel-note` is the documented panel wrapper (`admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`), which the core class-name check does not recognise.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors on either zip (GitHub zip: only the expected updater findings). Library CDNs were dropped from the "not worth listing" hosts, since they still receive visitors' IP addresses; the security hosts kept there (reCAPTCHA, Turnstile) carry a `phpcs:ignore` with the reason.

GitHub Actions did not start on this PR: the account's Actions billing reports failed payments or a spending limit. The local runs above cover the same jobs (lint, smoke test on 7.1/PHP 8.3 and 6.2/PHP 7.4, release build, preflight, Plugin Check).

Not in this PR (follow-ups): screenshots and banner art for WordPress.org, Scan now button and first-run guide, lightbox embeds added after page load.

title: GH#7: hold back dynamically inserted scripts and iframes
body:
## Summary

Resolves #7.

- Guard dynamic script/iframe sources and common DOM insertions before requests start; observe added nodes for placeholders.
- Reuse the existing consent choice, banner, dialog and release paths.
- Preserve exclusions, Google advanced mode and editor bypasses.

Adds compact URL match fragments from the existing service list (retaining paths on shared hosts), translated placeholder copy, settings exclusions and editor-bypass activation. No per-view reporting or visitor-dependent HTML.

Dynamic-only limitations are documented: inline-only injected code, shadow roots, other documents, `document.write`/range APIs, `srcdoc`, fetch/XHR and saved native methods require integrations to consult consent. Optimizers must not delay the consent head script. No legal or region defaults change.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: medium.
- Level: runtime-verified, head `7bd6aa6451856400945d36545cbf6c76128997cd`.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS and PHPStan pass; no JS build is configured. The final URL-filter tweak also passed scoped PHP syntax/PHPCS and final browser rerun.
- Isolated WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3, headless Brave, Europe/London: dynamic YouTube iframe and GA script make **zero requests before consent**. Load releases YouTube only; Accept releases GA exactly once. Reject never loads either.
- Verified appendChild, append/prepend, nested DocumentFragment, replaceChild, live innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML and connected iframe src/property or setAttribute changes. Placeholders and the banner appear on a previously empty page; it stays hidden without matches.
- Verified original script `onload` and addEventListener callbacks fire once; changed held URLs release only the latest source; unmatched and empty sources discard stale blocking metadata/wrappers. Opt-out discovers an allowed service for the notice; ignored/JSON scripts retain their behavior. Actual settings for Never hold back and Google advanced mode permit the excluded services.
- No browser pageerrors; WordPress debug log empty. Disposable site removed and preview-browser session logged out.
- Nine-sample no-match insertion probe: median **0.5 ms** for 1,000 insertions with dynamic guards versus **0.4 ms** without; banner stayed hidden. This bounded microbenchmark is not a whole-site performance guarantee.

## Acceptance and review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Dynamically inserted script/iframe held before requests | Zero-request browser checks above |
| Placeholder and consent release use existing UI | Load/Reject/Accept and callback checks above |
| No JS errors; negligible no-match work | Empty pageerror list and insertion comparison |
| Config remains compact and page-cache safe | Shared URL fragments only; server activation flag, no per-visitor HTML |

## Summary

Resolves #44

- Continue site-local consent recording when the source adapter finds existing record rows
- Use prepared `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` probes without reading record contents
- Leave hosted providers unchanged and reuse the normal dry-run/import/undo paths

## Files and reference

The six adapters in `includes/migrate/` follow the existing Complianz `consent_days` settings mapping. README.md, readme.txt and changelog.txt explain the changed behavior. No shared core files, hosted adapters or import/undo machinery change.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: medium (bounded admin/CLI database reads); testing level: runtime-verified
- Head: ffa220cb72a7d9e508366d31a6fcaae84f50a7ac
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all checks pass (PHP/JavaScript syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS, PHPStan); no JavaScript build is configured
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: passes on WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3 with 10,001 posts and 30,002 meta rows, default/all-enabled settings, HTTP/admin requests, query checks and uninstall
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no unexpected errors for either release zip; WordPress.org zip has zero errors or warnings; GitHub zip has only documented shared-updater findings
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: zero errors; readme size passes. Nine warnings concern the intentional Unreleased headings (two), existing listing slug/starter assets (six), and the unchanged release tag (one). No publication is requested; existing launch items remain outside this task
- Disposable `scripts/test-site.sh` environments: 84 assertions pass on each of WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.3 and WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4, exercising the actual migration API and settings store against MariaDB
- Per adapter: missing/empty/populated tables, one bounded query without reading row contents, read-only plan, import on, repeat `changed:false`, undo off, re-import, subsequent owner off choice and already-on choice
- Negative cases: Complianz data requests, Real Cookie Banner revisions and WPConsent Do Not Track requests alone do not turn recording on; hosted Cookiebot/iubenda/Termly settings remain unchanged
- Installed and activated actual Complianz Free 7.5.6: CLI plan contains no consent-record setting when no local records table exists
- Debug logs remain empty

Coverage limits: row-presence cases use disposable minimal source-table fixtures, not visitor-generated records from licensed Premium/Pro installations. No new committed test harness or test-only product interface is added.

## Acceptance self-review

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complianz local rows appear in dry run and enable recording | Satisfied | Populated `cmplz_statistics` fixture; plan/import assertions on both supported runtime boundaries |
| Undo restores recording off | Satisfied | Real import journal and undo assertions for all six adapters |
| Complianz Free without local records leaves recording unchanged | Satisfied | Actual Free 7.5.6 activation and CLI plan; missing/empty-table assertions |
| Repeat import reports `changed:false` | Satisfied | All six adapters on both runtimes |
| Preserve subsequent owner choice | Satisfied | Undo after owner switches off; already-on values excluded from plan |
| Hosted records unchanged; no record contents read | Satisfied | Hosted negative cases and captured exact `SELECT 1 FROM ... LIMIT 1` probes |

Self-review bundle: `e9f64cb9759caaf3c10eff23c948f8d511200be80427af0e30e6aaca6d086bbb`; injection scan clean. No material defect found in direct diff review. The final commit only shortens the migration FAQ to keep readme.txt at 10,156 bytes (below the 10 KB gate); the PHP artifacts are identical to those runtime-tested on both versions.

## Decisions

- Require row evidence rather than guessing undocumented Pro settings
- Ignore request/revision-only tables, which are kept by cleanup but are not consent choices
- Keep notes in present-tense import wording so a read-only preview does not falsely claim it already changed the setting
- Reuse normal default-only import and changed-since undo behavior

body:
Resolves #155

## Summary

- **Privacy policy** (new, off by default, Policies tab): `seoprocookieconsent/privacy-policy` block and `[spcc_privacy_policy]` shortcode in `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-privacy.php`, built like Terms. Renders a general plain-English policy from the owner's answers. The wording draws on what the owner's existing site policies cover, written generically (no copied names, addresses or site-specific claims):
  - who is responsible and what the policy covers (Country, when given, is named here and under Complaints);
  - what is collected, by category and how (given, automatic, from others), with aggregated data, information needed to provide a service, and public comments;
  - each purpose with its legal basis, legitimate interests, marketing, and not selling personal information or giving it to others for their own marketing; if a visitor allows marketing cookies, the advertising services that set them may also use what they collect for their own purposes;
  - AI; cookies, listing the banner's cookie kinds and, with Cookie consent on, what the banner does: holding back, how long a choice is remembered (`consent_days`), Global Privacy Control, and with **Keep consent records** on, what a record holds and how long it is kept (the longer of `consent_days` and `consent_records_days`, as `SEOProCookieConsent_Records` applies);
  - sharing, payment pages, international transfers, how retention is decided, security, each right with identity checks and a reply within four weeks, complaints, children, other websites, changes and contact.
  - Business, country and contact fall back to the Terms answers. Nothing renders until a name and contact exist. Optional data protection registration and main service providers; Your own wording replaces the suggestions. `seoprocookieconsent_privacy_sections` filter, same shape as `seoprocookieconsent_terms_sections`.
- **AI section in the privacy policy**, two switches; with both off the section is left out:
  - `privacy_ai` (on by default), the owner's own use: AI services from several providers help develop the site and may also help answer questions and support requests; when AI helps with a message, personal information is removed, as far as possible, from what is sent, so only the general content is processed.
  - `privacy_ai_features` (new, **off** by default), AI that visitors use on the site (chat assistant, AI search, AI forms or tools): what they type, upload or submit goes **in full** to the AI provider, without personal information removed, so they should leave out personal, sensitive or confidential information; the provider handles it under its own terms and may process it abroad; any copy kept (such as chat history) is handled as the policy describes. The setting asks owners to say the same where the feature is used.
  - Both: where possible, services and settings that do not train on what is sent; AI makes no decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
- **Terms: much fuller suggested wording** (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-terms.php`): accepting the terms and other agreements, changes, who can use the site, acceptable use, accounts and passwords, content visitors post (they keep ownership), intellectual property and downloads, links and affiliate links, information and no professional advice, availability and security, responsibility for loss or damage (never limited for death, personal injury or fraud; foreseeable loss for consumers; a cap at the price paid for business users), suspending access, privacy and communications, accessibility and complaints, Your rights, and general provisions.
  - **No scraping, with evidence** (after the acceptable-use list, which already bans automated collection): the owner may use measures that detect and block automated access, may mark content and data uniquely (data fingerprinting) and include decoy details that appear nowhere else (canary tokens) to recognise copies and trace who made them, and may keep what these record as evidence, including in legal action against unauthorised copying and to recover costs where the law allows. "May", because sites differ; it is data fingerprinting, not browser or device fingerprinting. The Privacy policy already covers security records and legal claims as purposes.
  - **Complaints**: contact us first with any complaint or concern; if it cannot be resolved and the visitor chooses mediation, we endeavour to take part in good faith where the concern is legitimate. Mediation is voluntary and does not affect legal rights, including going to a regulator or the courts. **No arbitration clause** (pre-dispute arbitration generally cannot bind UK consumers).
  - **Orders and payment** follows What we offer, only when `terms_sells` is answered.
  - **Governing law**, only when `terms_country` is filled: that place's law and courts, with consumers keeping the mandatory protection of the law where they live. The Country setting's description now asks for the legal system's name ("England and Wales", "Jersey"), not a code.
  - Filtered sections now come before Information on this website (still before AI-assisted services and Your rights). `migrate()` and `DB_VERSION` are unchanged.
- **AI section in the terms** (`terms_ai`, on by default), before Our responsibility and Your rights: AI helps develop the site and services and may also help answer questions; visitors accept that services are provided with AI support and should check what is provided for correctness, themselves or with their own AI tools, before relying on it.
- **Shared document base** (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-document.php`, plugin-own, not a core file): abstract `SEOProCookieConsent_Document` registers the shortcode and block, renders Your own wording or the suggestions, filtered sections and the questions under the switch, and `part()` (a heading, then paragraphs and lists). Terms and Privacy policy extend it.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt` (unchanged, 10,234 of 10,240 bytes), `changelog.txt` (Unreleased), `docs/architecture.md`, `AGENTS.md`; `languages/seoprocookieconsent.pot` refreshed. No core files changed.

title: GH#158: hold Meta Pixel for WordPress until Meta Pixel is allowed
body:
## What

Meta Pixel for WordPress (Meta's own plugin, 5.2+) broke Cookie consent in three ways:

1. It set the `_fbp`/`_fbc` marketing cookies from PHP on a visitor's first page, before any choice (it runs when its file loads, before this plugin).
2. Its server events (Conversions API) were not held.
3. The pixel never started, even after consent: its new inline `FacebookSignal.init()/initPixel()` and `fbq('track'…)` ran at once and threw a ReferenceError, because the `fbevents.js` loader was held.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-meta.php` (new). It runs only when Meta's plugin is active and Cookie consent is on.
  - `before_conversions_api_event_sent` sends server events only when Meta's state cookie `wc_facebook_signals_state` is `active`. Cron, WP-CLI and wp-admin screens (Meta's test events) are not affected. Meta's background send (admin-post) and admin-ajax carry the visitor's cookies, so they follow the same rule.
  - The `_fbp`/`_fbc` `Set-Cookie` headers Meta sent before this plugin loaded are removed for a visitor without `active`.
- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: `spcc.syncMeta()` sets `wc_facebook_signals_state=active` only while Meta Pixel is allowed, and removes it otherwise. It runs in the head before Meta's scripts. `assets/js/spcc.js` `signal()` calls it after each choice, before releasing held scripts.
- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-services.php`: the `meta-pixel` patterns now include `facebooksignal.initpixel(`, `fbq('track` and `fbq("track`, so the inline start-up and tracking code is held with its loader and runs after it. `_fbc` is added to the cookies removed when consent is withdrawn.
- This change never uses Meta's `held` state or its `facebook_signals_held` filter. In the held state Meta renders different HTML: it queues events for a release request instead of calling `fbq('track'…)`. A page cache filled by such a request would lose the page view for visitors who allowed Meta Pixel. Pages now look the same to every visitor. `docs/architecture.md` → Signals to other code explains this.
- README, changelog and the POT (line references only) are updated.

## Verification

Local test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3) with `official-facebook-pixel` 5.2.2, a dummy pixel ID and Conversions API on:

- **Server cookies.** With no cookie and `?fbclid=`, the response has no `Set-Cookie` for `_fbp`/`_fbc`. With `wc_facebook_signals_state=active`, both are set.
- **Server events.** A probe of `before_conversions_api_event_sent` returned:

  | Request | No cookie | `active` | `held` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Front end | 0 | 1 | – |
  | admin-post (async path) | 0 | 1 | – |
  | admin-ajax | 0 | – | 0 |
  | WP-CLI | 1 | – | – |

- **Same HTML.** The Meta parts of the HTML are identical with and without the cookie. Both are Meta's non-held render.
- **Browser** (Playwright, Europe/London, opt-in):
  - On first load there are no requests to `connect.facebook.net` or `facebook.com`, no cookies and no console errors.
  - After Accept all: `wc_facebook_signals_state=active`, `fbevents.js` loads, the pixel initialises (`_pixelInitialized=true`) and `tr?…ev=PageView` is sent. There are no errors.
  - After a reload, the pixel initialises again and PageView is sent.
  - After Reject all, the page reloads. `wc_facebook_signals_state`, `_fbp` and `_fbc` are removed, `fbq` is undefined and there are no Facebook requests.
  - When a page loads with a stale `wc_facebook_signals_state=held`, the cookie is removed.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: no errors after the POT refresh. The warnings are the usual release-time ones: Unreleased section, slug note, starter core-file drift and the tag on main.

Out of scope, not changed:

- Meta's `<noscript>` image pixel. It still fires for visitors without JavaScript, as before.
- Facebook for WooCommerce. It is not installed on any checked site, and its code was not reviewed.

Resolves #158

title: GH#181: fix: speed: read hex and rgb() button colours without a canvas

## What and why

Resolves #181.

The button-contrast check (#68) read every colour through a 1×1 canvas. That runs on every page view, and the first canvas draw and read-back in a page is slow (a software canvas is set up).
